chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When a man sneezes three times, say 'Bismillah' for him, then leave him (if he sneezes again).
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling when someone sneezes three times?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Zurarah to Imam al-Baqir, clarifies the specific etiquette of responding to sneezing by reciting 'Bismillah' only once, even if the person sneezes multiple times. It establishes a limit to the customary response, preventing excessive repetition and distinguishing this practice from the more common 'Alhamdulillah' response found in other traditions. This ruling highlights the precision of Shia fiqh in daily social interactions and the importance of adhering to the Imams' specific instructions on ritual etiquette.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhassin Bin Ahmad, from Aban Bin usman, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When a man sneezes three (times), so Name (Allah<sup>azwj</sup> in response) and leave him (if he sneezes any more)’.
en.sarwar: 27. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhsin ibn Ahmad from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from Zurara from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “
If one sneezes three times, the special expressions for this purpose should be said only up to three times and thereafter should be left alone.”
